record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: For a finitely generated group G, is the first L2-Betti number always equal to cost(G) - 1, and is the Fixed Price Conjecture true, meaning that every essentially free probability-measure-preserving action of G on a standard Borel space has cost equal to the cost of G itself?

evidence.quote: Question 9.5. Let G be a finitely generated group. Do we have b(2)1 (G) = cost(G) − 1 and is the Fixed Price Conjecture true? (The Fixed Price Conjecture predicts that the cost of every standard action of G, i.e., an essentially free G-action on a standard Borel space with G-invariant probability measure, is equal to the cost of G.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finitely generated countable group. A standard probability-measure-preserving action of G is an action of G on a standard Borel probability space (X, μ) by measurable, measure-preserving transformations such that the action is essentially free (the stabilizer of μ-almost every point is trivial). For such an action, the cost of the associated orbit equivalence relation R on (X, μ) is defined as the infimum over all generating graphings Φ = (φ_i) of R (i.e., countable families of partial measure-preserving isomorphisms whose induced equivalence relation equals R almost everywhere) of the total measure Σ_i μ(dom(φ_i)). The cost of G, denoted cost(G), is the infimum of the costs of all such essentially free p.m.p. actions of G. Let b_1^{(2)}(G) denote the first L²-Betti number of G.

(a) Is it true that for every finitely generated group G one has
   b_1^{(2)}(G) = cost(G) − 1 ?

(b) (Fixed Price Conjecture) Is it true that for every finitely generated group G, every essentially free standard p.m.p. action of G has the same cost, equal to cost(G)?
artifact.status_search_result: Both questions are long-standing open problems originally posed by Gaboriau. The equality cost(G) = 1 + b_1^{(2)}(G) (with the known inequality cost(G) ≥ 1 + b_1^{(2)}(G)) and the Fixed Price Conjecture remain open in general, although they are confirmed for various classes (free groups, amenable groups, groups with infinite center, free products, Kazhdan property (T) groups have cost 1). Recent literature continues to treat these as open.

status_evidence.title: Around the orbit equivalence theory, measure equivalence, cost (Gaboriau lectures)
status_evidence.snippet: Gaboriau proved cost(Γ) ≥ 1 + β₁(Γ) and asked whether equality always holds; the Fixed Price Conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The cost vs first L²-Betti number equality and Fixed Price Conjecture are stated as open problems.

status_evidence.title: Kazhdan groups have cost 1, Inventiones Math.
status_evidence.snippet: Every countably infinite group with Kazhdan's property (T) has cost 1, answering a question of Gaboriau.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress confirms fixed-price-type statements for Kazhdan groups but general conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Point processes, cost, and the growth of rank in locally compact groups
status_evidence.snippet: Connections of cost with L²-Betti numbers and the Poisson process approach to Gaboriau's cost vs L² Betti problem are discussed as open.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats the cost = 1 + β₁ problem as open.
